functions.name: wm_SemInit
functions.description: Initializes a wolfMQTT binary semaphore instance used for multi-thread synchronization when WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD is enabled. The wm_Sem type is platform-specific (e.g., POSIX mutex/cond pair, Windows HANDLE, FreeRTOS SemaphoreHandle_t, etc.). Returns an int status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: Available only when WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD is defined at compile time (function is declared inside an #ifdef WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD block).
Argument s must be a non-NULL pointer to a wm_Sem object.
Must be called before wm_SemLock, wm_SemUnlock, or wm_SemFree on the same object.
Platform-specific constraints may apply because wm_Sem differs by platform (POSIX, Windows, FreeRTOS, etc.).
Return value semantics are not specified in this header; callers should check for non-zero/negative as failure per typical library patterns, but exact codes are unknown.

functions.name: wm_SemFree
functions.description: Releases and cleans up resources associated with a previously initialized wolfMQTT binary semaphore. Intended to be called when the semaphore is no longer needed. Returns an int status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: Available only when WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD is defined at compile time.
Argument s must be a non-NULL pointer to a previously initialized wm_Sem (initialized via wm_SemInit).
Should not be called while other threads are using or waiting on the semaphore (inferred from typical semaphore lifecycle).
Return value semantics are not specified in this header; exact success/failure codes are unknown.

functions.name: wm_SemLock
functions.description: Acquires (locks) the wolfMQTT binary semaphore to enter a critical section. On many platforms this will block the caller until the semaphore becomes available. Returns an int status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: Available only when WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD is defined at compile time.
Argument s must be a non-NULL pointer to a wm_Sem that has been successfully initialized via wm_SemInit.
May block until the semaphore is available (behavior inferred from typical semaphore semantics).
Caller should pair each successful wm_SemLock with a subsequent wm_SemUnlock on the same object before destruction (inferred).
Return value semantics are not specified in this header; exact success/failure codes are unknown.

functions.name: wm_SemUnlock
functions.description: Releases (unlocks) a previously locked wolfMQTT binary semaphore, allowing other waiting threads to proceed. Returns an int status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: Available only when WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD is defined at compile time.
Argument s must be a non-NULL pointer to a wm_Sem that has been successfully initialized via wm_SemInit.
Should only be called to release a semaphore previously acquired (locked) by the caller (inferred from typical semaphore usage and potential platform restrictions).
Must not be called after wm_SemFree on the same object.
Return value semantics are not specified in this header; exact success/failure codes are unknown.

functions.name: MqttSocket_TlsSocketReceive
functions.signature: int MqttSocket_TlsSocketReceive(WOLFSSL* ssl, char* buf, int sz, void* ptr);
functions.description: wolfSSL I/O receive callback used by wolfMQTT’s TLS layer to read encrypted data from the underlying MQTT socket. Intended to be registered with wolfSSL (e.g., via wolfSSL_SetIORecv) when the application creates its own WOLFSSL_CTX/WOLFSSL in the MQTT TLS callback. Typical usage is internal to wolfSSL during the TLS handshake and record processing; applications generally do not call this directly. Return value and error handling follow wolfSSL I/O callback conventions. Details of the context held in ptr are internal/opaque to wolfMQTT and not documented here.
requirements: This symbol is available only when ENABLE_MQTT_TLS is defined and neither ENABLE_MQTT_CURL nor ENABLE_MQTT_WEBSOCKET are defined (compile-time condition).
ssl must be a valid, initialized WOLFSSL session associated with the MQTT connection.
buf must be non-null and point to a writable buffer with capacity of at least sz bytes.
sz must be a positive integer; zero or negative sizes are invalid.
ptr must be a valid non-null context pointer as expected by wolfMQTT’s TLS integration (opaque to callers; typically provided when registering the callback).

Caller should expect wolfSSL-style semantics: the function returns the number of bytes received on success; negative values indicate an error per wolfSSL I/O callback conventions (exact error codes are managed by wolfSSL).
The underlying transport/socket associated with ssl must be connected/usable when this function is invoked (usually enforced by wolfSSL during handshake/record I/O).

functions.name: MqttSocket_TlsSocketSend
functions.signature: int MqttSocket_TlsSocketSend(WOLFSSL* ssl, char* buf, int sz, void* ptr);
functions.description: wolfSSL I/O send callback used by wolfMQTT’s TLS layer to write encrypted data to the underlying MQTT socket. Intended to be registered with wolfSSL (e.g., via wolfSSL_SetIOSend) when the application creates its own WOLFSSL_CTX/WOLFSSL in the MQTT TLS callback. Typically invoked internally by wolfSSL during handshake and record transmission; applications generally do not call this directly. Return value and error handling follow wolfSSL I/O callback conventions. Details of the context held in ptr are internal/opaque to wolfMQTT and not documented here.
requirements: This symbol is available only when ENABLE_MQTT_TLS is defined and neither ENABLE_MQTT_CURL nor ENABLE_MQTT_WEBSOCKET are defined (compile-time condition).
ssl must be a valid, initialized WOLFSSL session associated with the MQTT connection.
buf must be non-null and point to at least sz bytes of readable data to send.
sz must be a positive integer; zero or negative sizes are invalid.
ptr must be a valid non-null context pointer as expected by wolfMQTT’s TLS integration (opaque to callers; typically provided when registering the callback).

Caller should expect wolfSSL-style semantics: the function returns the number of bytes sent on success; negative values indicate an error per wolfSSL I/O callback conventions (exact error codes are managed by wolfSSL).
The underlying transport/socket associated with ssl must be connected/usable when this function is invoked (usually enforced by wolfSSL during handshake/record I/O).

functions.name: MqttPacket_TypeDesc
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for the given MQTT packet type (e.g., CONNECT, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE). Intended for diagnostics/logging. Note: if the library is compiled with WOLFMQTT_NO_ERROR_STRINGS defined, this symbol is not emitted as a function; instead, MqttPacket_TypeDesc(x) is a macro that expands to the literal "not compiled in".
requirements: The library must be built without WOLFMQTT_NO_ERROR_STRINGS to call/link the actual function; otherwise the name is a macro to the literal string "not compiled in".
Argument packet_type should be a valid value of the MqttPacketType enumeration; passing unknown values may yield an implementation-defined/unknown description.
The returned pointer is a pointer to constant, null-terminated text and must not be modified or freed by the caller.

functions.name: MqttClient_Flags
functions.signature: WOLFMQTT_API word32 MqttClient_Flags(struct _MqttClient *client,  word32 mask, word32 flags);
functions.description: Set and clear client flags atomically on an MqttClient. Intended to be called by the application before MqttClient_NetConnect to configure behavior (e.g., TLS/DTLS). Returns the resulting flags value.
requirements: client must point to a valid MqttClient structure (initialized or being prepared).
mask indicates which bits to clear; flags indicates which bits to set (values are from enum MqttClientFlags).
Call before MqttClient_NetConnect, per note in comment.

functions.name: MqttClient_Init
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API int MqttClient_Init(
    MqttClient *client,
    MqttNet *net,
    MqttMsgCb msg_cb,
    byte *tx_buf, int tx_buf_len,
    byte *rx_buf, int rx_buf_len,
    int cmd_timeout_ms);
functions.description: Initialize an MqttClient object with network callbacks, message callback, TX/RX buffers, and command timeout. Must be called before other client operations.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer; structure may be uninitialized on entry.
net must point to an MqttNet initialized with callback pointers and context.
tx_buf must point to a writable buffer of length tx_buf_len; tx_buf_len must be > 0.
rx_buf must point to a writable buffer of length rx_buf_len; rx_buf_len must be > 0.
msg_cb should be a valid function pointer if incoming publishes are expected.
cmd_timeout_ms is the maximum command wait timeout in milliseconds; must be >= 0.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_BAD_ARG; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_DeInit
functions.description: Clean up resources allocated to an MqttClient. Call when done with the client to release resources.
requirements: client must point to an MqttClient previously initialized by MqttClient_Init.
After calling, the client must not be used unless re-initialized.

functions.name: MqttClient_SetDisconnectCallback
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API int MqttClient_SetDisconnectCallback(
    MqttClient *client,
    MqttDisconnectCb discb,
    void* ctx);
functions.description: Register a disconnect callback and user context, invoked on network/disconnect events. Available only when compiled with WOLFMQTT_DISCONNECT_CB.
requirements: Requires compile-time define WOLFMQTT_DISCONNECT_CB to be enabled; otherwise this API is not available.
client must be a valid pointer; structure may be uninitialized on entry (per comment).
discb must be a valid MqttDisconnectCb function pointer.
ctx is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_BAD_ARG; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_SetPropertyCallback
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API int MqttClient_SetPropertyCallback(
    MqttClient *client,
    MqttPropertyCb propCb,
    void* ctx);
functions.description: Register a property callback and user context for MQTT v5 properties. Available only when compiled with WOLFMQTT_PROPERTY_CB (which requires WOLFMQTT_V5).
requirements: Requires compile-time defines WOLFMQTT_PROPERTY_CB and WOLFMQTT_V5; otherwise this API is not available.
client must be a valid pointer; structure may be uninitialized on entry (per comment).
propCb must be a valid MqttPropertyCb function pointer.
ctx is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_BAD_ARG; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_Connect
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT CONNECT and wait (blocking) for CONNACK. Establishes an MQTT session with the broker using parameters in MqttConnect.
requirements: client must be initialized via MqttClient_Init and the network connected via MqttClient_NetConnect.
connect must point to an MqttConnect structure initialized with desired connect parameters.
This call blocks waiting on MqttNet.read; ensure underlying network is operational or set appropriate timeouts.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*; caller should handle errors.

functions.name: MqttClient_Publish
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT PUBLISH and, for QoS > 0, wait for the corresponding acknowledgments. If payload exceeds buffer size, may be called successively to transmit the full payload.
requirements: client must be connected (successful MqttClient_Connect) and initialized.
publish must point to an MqttPublish structure initialized with message data (topic, QoS, payload buffers).
For QoS 1: function waits for PUBACK; for QoS 2: waits for PUBREC, sends PUBREL, then waits for PUBCOMP.
This call waits for MqttNet.read to complete, may block until timeout; in non-blocking mode may return MQTT_CODE_CONTINUE.
MqttPublish and MqttMessage are the same structure; ensure fields are set consistently.
Caller must check return code for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS, MQTT_CODE_CONTINUE (non-blocking), or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*.

functions.name: MqttClient_Publish_ex
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API int MqttClient_Publish_ex(
    MqttClient *client,
    MqttPublish *publish,
    MqttPublishCb pubCb);
functions.description: Publish with a data-supply callback. Encodes and sends PUBLISH and, for QoS > 0, waits for acknowledgments. The callback fills the transmit payload in chunks, allowing small TX buffers.
requirements: client must be initialized and connected.
publish must be initialized with message metadata; the callback will populate publish.buffer and related fields for each chunk.
pubCb must be a valid function that returns >= 0 on success and provides payload pieces as requested.
Blocks waiting on MqttNet.read, times out, or may return MQTT_CODE_CONTINUE in non-blocking mode.
For QoS 1 and 2, waits for the documented ACK sequences.
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_Publish_WriteOnly
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API int MqttClient_Publish_WriteOnly(
    MqttClient *client,
    MqttPublish *publish,
    MqttPublishCb pubCb);
functions.description: Write-only variant of publish for multithreaded use. Performs only writes; a separate thread must handle read/ACK processing using MqttClient_WaitMessage_ex. Same behavior regarding QoS acknowledgments, but reads are externalized. Available only with WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD.
requirements: Requires compile-time define WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD.
client must be initialized and connected.
Another thread must process ACKs by calling MqttClient_WaitMessage_ex.
publish must be initialized; pubCb must be a valid callback supplying payload chunks.
May block waiting on MqttNet.read to complete, timeout, or return MQTT_CODE_CONTINUE if non-blocking (per note).
Caller must check return code for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS, MQTT_CODE_CONTINUE, or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*.

functions.name: MqttClient_Subscribe
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT SUBSCRIBE and wait (blocking) for SUBACK. Subscribes to one or more topics with desired QoS.
requirements: client must be initialized and connected.
subscribe must point to an MqttSubscribe initialized with subscription topic list and desired QoS.
This is a blocking call that waits on MqttNet.read.
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_Unsubscribe
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT UNSUBSCRIBE and wait (blocking) for UNSUBACK.
requirements: client must be initialized and connected.
unsubscribe must point to an MqttUnsubscribe initialized with topic list.
This is a blocking call that waits on MqttNet.read.
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_Ping
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT PINGREQ and wait (blocking) for PINGRESP. Keeps the connection alive.
requirements: client must be initialized and connected.
This is a blocking call that waits on MqttNet.read.
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_Ping_ex
functions.description: Ping variant that accepts an MqttPing structure and can be used with non-blocking applications. Sends PINGREQ and waits for PINGRESP.
requirements: client must be initialized and connected.
ping must point to an MqttPing structure (caller-managed).
This call may block waiting on MqttNet.read (per note).
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_Auth
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT v5 AUTH packet and wait for the response. Used for enhanced authentication flows. Available only when WOLFMQTT_V5 is enabled.
requirements: Requires compile-time define WOLFMQTT_V5.
client must be initialized and connected.
auth must point to an initialized MqttAuth structure.
This is a blocking call that waits on MqttNet.read.
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_PropsAdd
functions.description: Allocate a new MQTT v5 property node and add it to the head of a property list to be attached to a subsequent packet command.
requirements: Requires compile-time define WOLFMQTT_V5.
head must be a valid pointer to a MqttProp* (pointer-to-head).
Must be called prior to the packet command that will use the properties.
Returns a pointer to the new MqttProp on success or NULL on error (implied by typical allocation semantics); caller should check result.

functions.name: MqttClient_PropsFree
functions.description: Free a property list previously created for a packet command. Deallocates all nodes starting at head.
requirements: Requires compile-time define WOLFMQTT_V5.
head may be NULL or a valid list head; frees the list pointed to by head.
Must be called after the packet command that used MqttClient_PropsAdd.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or -1 on error (and sets errno); caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_Disconnect
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT DISCONNECT (no response expected). Non-blocking; attempts to send via MqttNet.write.
requirements: client must be initialized; typically called when connected.
This is non-blocking and does not wait for a server response.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_Disconnect_ex
functions.description: Encode and send an MQTT DISCONNECT with optional parameters (MQTT v5) and no response expected. Non-blocking; attempts to send via MqttNet.write. When WOLFMQTT_USE_CB_ON_DISCONNECT is enabled, may trigger the disconnect callback.
requirements: client must be initialized; typically called when connected.
disconnect may be NULL (explicitly allowed) or point to a valid MqttDisconnect structure.
This is non-blocking and does not wait for a server response.
If WOLFMQTT_USE_CB_ON_DISCONNECT is defined, the disconnect callback may be triggered.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_WaitMessage
functions.description: Block waiting for incoming MQTT packets up to timeout_ms. Incoming PUBLISH messages are delivered via the MqttMsgCb set at initialization.
requirements: client must be initialized and connected.
timeout_ms specifies milliseconds until read timeout; must be >= 0.
Blocks waiting on MqttNet.read.
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_WaitMessage_ex
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API int MqttClient_WaitMessage_ex(
    MqttClient *client,
    MqttObject *msg,
    int timeout_ms);
functions.description: Block waiting for incoming MQTT packets, populating the provided MqttObject. Incoming PUBLISH messages are delivered via the registered message callback.
requirements: client must be initialized and connected.
msg must point to a valid MqttObject structure owned by the caller (per non-blocking note in related APIs).
timeout_ms specifies milliseconds until read timeout; must be >= 0.
Blocks waiting on MqttNet.read.
Caller must check return code for success or error.

functions.name: MqttClient_CancelMessage
functions.description: Cancel an MQTT object previously submitted in multithreaded or non-blocking modes. Allows aborting an in-flight operation.
requirements: Available only when compiled with WOLFMQTT_MULTITHREAD or WOLFMQTT_NONBLOCK.
client must be initialized.
msg must point to the MqttObject to cancel (previously submitted).
This is a blocking function that will wait for MqttNet.read (per note).
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_IsMessageActive
functions.description: In non-blocking mode, check whether the given message has a pending read or write (state not MQTT_MSG_BEGIN). Assumes the caller owns the object.
requirements: Available only when compiled with WOLFMQTT_NONBLOCK.
client must be initialized.
msg must be a pointer to a valid MqttObject owned by the caller (per note).
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_NetConnect
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API int MqttClient_NetConnect(
    MqttClient *client,
    const char *host,
    word16 port,
    int timeout_ms,
    int use_tls,
    MqttTlsCb cb);
functions.description: Open the underlying network connection to the broker and optionally establish TLS/DTLS. If use_tls is non-zero, the MqttTlsCb is invoked to configure TLS settings.
requirements: client must be initialized (MqttClient_Init) and contain a valid MqttNet with callbacks.
host must be a valid server address string.
port may be zero to use defaults; otherwise must be a valid broker port.
timeout_ms is the read timeout in milliseconds; must be >= 0.
use_tls non-zero enables TLS; zero uses plain TCP/UDP as configured.
cb should be a valid TLS configuration callback when use_tls != 0.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_NetDisconnect
functions.description: Close the underlying network connection to the broker.
requirements: client must be initialized; typically called after MqttClient_Disconnect or on error.
Returns MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_*; caller should check return value.

functions.name: MqttClient_GetProtocolVersion
functions.description: Return the numeric MQTT protocol version negotiated for the current connection: 4 for v3.1.1 or 5 for v5.
requirements: client must be initialized; typically called after successful connect.
Return value is 4 (v3.1.1) or 5 (v5).

functions.name: MqttClient_GetProtocolVersionString
functions.description: Return a human-readable string for the connected protocol version: "v3.1.1" or "v5".
requirements: client must be initialized; typically called after successful connect.
Returned pointer refers to an internal or static string; treat as read-only.

functions.name: MqttClient_ReturnCodeToString
functions.signature:
WOLFMQTT_API const char* MqttClient_ReturnCodeToString(
    int return_code);
functions.description: Translate a wolfMQTT API return code into a descriptive string. If compiled with WOLFMQTT_NO_ERROR_STRINGS, this function is not available and a macro returning "not compiled in" is defined instead.
requirements: Available only when WOLFMQTT_NO_ERROR_STRINGS is not defined; otherwise the symbol is a macro, not a function.
return_code must be a value returned by a WOLFMQTT_API function.
Returned pointer is a constant string; do not modify.

functions.name: SN_Packet_TypeDesc
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for a given MQTT-SN packet type (SN_MsgType). Intended for diagnostics/logging. Note: This function is only available when error strings are compiled in; otherwise the name is defined as a macro that expands to the literal "not compiled in".
requirements: Must be compiled with MQTT-SN support (WOLFMQTT_SN defined).
Function form is only available when WOLFMQTT_NO_ERROR_STRINGS is not defined; if WOLFMQTT_NO_ERROR_STRINGS is defined, SN_Packet_TypeDesc is a macro returning the literal "not compiled in".
Argument packet_type should be a valid SN_MsgType value.
The returned const char* points to immutable storage; the caller must not modify or free it.

functions.name: SN_Client_SearchGW
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN SearchGW message to discover a gateway and waits for the gateway info response. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read. Use to discover a nearby MQTT-SN gateway prior to connecting.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
search must be a valid pointer to an SN_SearchGw structure initialized with hop radius (explicit).
This call blocks until a response or timeout via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or an MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Connect
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN CONNECT and waits for the CONNACK. If Will is enabled, the gateway may prompt for LWT Topic and Message; sending an empty will topic deletes any stored Will. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
connect must be a valid pointer to an SN_Connect structure initialized with connect parameters (explicit).
This call blocks until a response or timeout via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_WillTopicUpdate
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN Will Topic Update. Passing a NULL will deletes the stored Will topic and message on the server. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
will may be NULL to request deletion of stored Will, or a valid SN_Will structure initialized with topic/message parameters (explicit).
This call blocks until completion via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_WillMsgUpdate
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN Will Message Update. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read. Passing NULL is valid per comment, implying update/delete semantics per implementation.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
will may be NULL or a valid pointer to an SN_Will structure initialized with topic/message parameters (explicit).
This call blocks until completion via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Register
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN REGISTER and waits for the REGACK. Used by a client to request a topic ID for a topic name, or by a gateway to inform the client of an assigned topic ID. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
regist must be a valid pointer to an SN_Register structure (explicit).
This call blocks until a response via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_SetRegisterCallback
functions.signature: WOLFMQTT_API int SN_Client_SetRegisterCallback(MqttClient *client, SN_ClientRegisterCb regCb, void* ctx);
functions.description: Registers a callback to handle MQTT-SN REGISTER-related events, with an optional user context pointer. Useful to process dynamic topic ID assignments.
requirements: client may be uninitialized; any MqttClient pointer is acceptable (explicit: “uninitialized is okay”).
regCb must be a valid function pointer to a register callback (inferred from parameter type/usage).
ctx may be NULL or any user-provided pointer (inferred).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_BAD_ARG (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Publish
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN PUBLISH. If QoS > 0, waits for the appropriate acknowledgment sequence: QoS 1 waits for PUBLISH_ACK; QoS 2 waits for PUBREC, sends PUBREL, then waits for PUBCOMP. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read for QoS>0.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
publish must be a valid pointer to an SN_Publish structure initialized with message data (explicit).
SN_Publish uses the same structure layout as MqttMessage (explicit note).
For QoS > 0, caller should expect blocking behavior awaiting acknowledgments (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Subscribe
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN SUBSCRIBE and waits for the SUBACK containing the assigned topic ID. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
subscribe must be a valid pointer to an SN_Subscribe structure initialized with the subscription topic list and desired QoS (explicit).
This call blocks until a response via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Unsubscribe
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN UNSUBSCRIBE and waits for the UNSUBACK. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
unsubscribe must be a valid pointer to an SN_Unsubscribe structure initialized with topic ID (explicit).
This call blocks until a response via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Disconnect
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN DISCONNECT without additional parameters. Non-blocking; attempts to send via MqttNet.write. Can be used to cleanly end a session; duration-based asleep state is not provided in this overload.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
This call is non-blocking and attempts to send using MqttNet.write (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Disconnect_ex
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN DISCONNECT. Non-blocking; attempts to send via MqttNet.write. If a duration is set in the SN_Disconnect structure, the client can indicate it is entering the asleep state. Passing NULL for disconnect is valid.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
disconnect may be NULL or a valid pointer to an SN_Disconnect structure (explicit).
This call is non-blocking and attempts to send using MqttNet.write (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_Ping
functions.description: Encodes and sends an MQTT-SN PINGREQ and waits for PINGRESP. If the client is asleep and wants to notify the gateway it is waking, include the client ID in the ping request. Blocking; waits on MqttNet.read.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
ping may be NULL or a valid pointer to an SN_PingReq structure (explicit).
This call blocks until a response via MqttNet.read (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_WaitMessage
functions.description: Blocks waiting for incoming MQTT-SN packets for up to timeout_ms milliseconds. Incoming PUBLISH messages are delivered via the application callback set during MqttClient_Init.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
timeout_ms specifies the read timeout in milliseconds (explicit).
An incoming PUBLISH callback must be provided in MqttClient_Init to receive messages (explicit).
This call blocks and waits on MqttNet.read until timeout or a packet arrives (explicit).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

functions.name: SN_Client_WaitMessage_ex
functions.signature: WOLFMQTT_API int SN_Client_WaitMessage_ex(MqttClient *client, SN_Object* packet_obj, int timeout_ms);
functions.description: Blocks waiting for incoming MQTT-SN packets for up to timeout_ms milliseconds, optionally returning the received packet via packet_obj. Extended variant of SN_Client_WaitMessage that provides access to the packet object.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer to a MqttClient structure (inferred).
packet_obj should be a valid pointer to an SN_Object to receive the packet; behavior if NULL is not documented (inferred/unknown).
timeout_ms specifies the read timeout in milliseconds (explicit).
This call blocks and waits on MqttNet.read until timeout or a packet arrives (inferred from WaitMessage behavior).
Caller must check the return value for MQTT_CODE_SUCCESS or MQTT_CODE_ERROR_* (explicit).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: MQTT client identifier (UTF-8 string)
# Fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to populate MqttConnect.client_id.
# Generate interesting yet valid UTF-8 client IDs covering common broker rules:
# - Non-empty ASCII alnum
# - With separators (- _ . :)
# - Max-length boundaries (short, typical 23, larger like 64, 128, 256)
# - Variants starting with letter/digit
# - Unicode code points valid in UTF-8 (BMP and astral)
# - Pure digits, mixed, UUID-like, MAC-like, and random base64-like
# Returns bytes to seed the fuzzing input buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR will read from.

SAFE_SEPARATORS = "-_.:"
BASE_ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits

UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    (0x00A1, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 Supplement (excluding control)
    (0x0100, 0x017F),   # Latin Extended-A
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
    (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs (pick few to stay short)
    (0x1F300, 0x1F64F), # Emoji range subset
]

def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Pick a few codepoints from diverse ranges; ensure valid UTF-8
    cp_ranges = UNICODE_BLOCKS
    parts: List[str] = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(n):
        lo, hi = rng.choice(cp_ranges)
        cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        # Avoid surrogate area and control characters
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            cp = 0xE000
        try:
            parts.append(chr(cp))
        except ValueError:
            parts.append('x')
    return ''.join(parts)

def _uuid_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    hexs = string.hexdigits.lower()
    def seg(n):
        return ''.join(rng.choice(hexs[:16]) for _ in range(n))
    return f"{seg(8)}-{seg(4)}-{seg(4)}-{seg(4)}-{seg(12)}"

def _mac_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    hexs = '0123456789ABCDEF'
    return ':'.join(''.join(rng.choice(hexs) for _ in range(2)) for _ in range(6))

def _base64ish(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '+/_-'
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))
    # Add some padding-like chars sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s += '=' * rng.randint(0, 2)
    return s

def _bounded_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Prefer interesting boundaries typical for MQTT brokers
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 7, 10, 16, 23, 24, 30, 32, 40, 50, 64, 80, 96, 120, 128, 192, 255]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    return rng.randint(1, 255)

def _start_char(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common policy: start with letter or digit
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        return rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits)
    # Occasionally start with underscore or separator
    return rng.choice('_' + SAFE_SEPARATORS)

def _mix_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    pool = BASE_ALNUM + SAFE_SEPARATORS
    return ''.join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))

def _compose_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands: List[str] = []

    # 1) Simple alnum small
    cands.append('client')
    cands.append('c' + str(rng.randint(0, 999999)))

    # 2) Boundary lengths
    for L in (23, 24, 64, 128):
        head = _start_char(rng)
        rest = _mix_ascii(rng, max(0, L - len(head)))
        cands.append(head + rest)

    # 3) UUID-like
    cands.append(_uuid_like(rng))

    # 4) MAC-like
    cands.append(_mac_like(rng))

    # 5) Base64ish
    cands.append(_base64ish(rng, rng.randint(8, 22)))

    # 6) Mixed ASCII with separators
    L = _bounded_length(rng)
    cands.append(_start_char(rng) + _mix_ascii(rng, max(0, L - 1)))

    # 7) Pure digits
    cands.append(str(rng.randint(0, 10**12 - 1)))

    # 8) With periods and underscores
    parts = [
        ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(3,6)))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2,4))
    ]
    cands.append('_'.join(parts))
    cands.append('.'.join(parts))

    # 9) Unicode-only and mixed Unicode
    uni = _rand_unicode(rng)
    cands.append(uni)
    cands.append((_start_char(rng) + _mix_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3,8)) + uni)[:_bounded_length(rng)])

    # 10) Prefixes commonly used
    prefix = rng.choice(['mqtt-', 'client-', 'cid-', 'wolf-'])
    tail = _mix_ascii(rng, rng.randint(4, 16))
    cands.append(prefix + tail)

    # 11) Short minimal
    cands.append(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters))

    # 12) Long but <= 255
    L = _bounded_length(rng)
    cands.append(_start_char(rng) + _mix_ascii(rng, max(0, L - 1)))

    # Ensure all are non-empty and valid UTF-8 when encoded
    valid = []
    for s in cands:
        try:
            b = s.encode('utf-8')
            if 1 <= len(b) <= 255:
                valid.append(s)
        except UnicodeEncodeError:
            continue
    return valid

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    cands = _compose_candidates(rng)
    # Randomly pick one candidate, then optionally tweak length within bounds by appending safe chars
    s = rng.choice(cands) if cands else 'client'

    # Occasionally scale towards broker-friendly 23 chars
    target_lens = [23, 24, 32, 64]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        target = rng.choice(target_lens)
        # Append safe chars to reach target if shorter; if longer, trim
        bs = s.encode('utf-8')
        if len(bs) < target:
            add = _mix_ascii(rng, target - len(bs))
            s = s + add
        elif len(bs) > target:
            # Trim by bytes safely
            b = bs[:target]
            # Ensure no partial UTF-8: back up to start of codepoint
            while b and (b[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
                b = b[:-1]
            try:
                s = b.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
            except Exception:
                s = 'client'

    out = s.encode('utf-8')

    # Ensure final size constraint <= 4096
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
        # Avoid cutting inside UTF-8 sequence
        while out and (out[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            out = out[:-1]
    return out

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: MQTT topic string
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used for topics and payloads in the stubs.
# We will generate a bytes buffer that contains multiple NUL-terminated strings
# so the fuzzer can split/use them in order when calling FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times.
# Layout:
#   [count:1]
#   then count entries, each encoded as:
#       [kind:1][len:2-le][utf8-bytes][\x00]
# Kinds we produce:
#   0 = publish topic (no wildcards)
#   1 = subscribe filter (may contain +, #)
#   2 = payload (arbitrary UTF-8 printable and some binary-safe chars)
# The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for topic and payload. Providing a mix increases variety.
# The fuzzer framework will likely treat the buffer as a bag of strings; keeping them NUL-terminated is common.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SEG_SEP = "/"

PRINTABLE_SAFE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_."  # safe in topics
)

PAYLOAD_CHARS = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t\r\n"
)

# MQTT constraints helpers

def make_segment(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

def make_topic_publish(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # No wildcards. Depth from 1..6
    depth = rng.choices([1,2,3,4,5,6], weights=[2,3,3,2,1,1], k=1)[0]
    segs: List[str] = []
    for i in range(depth):
        # Occasionally include empty segment to test leading/trailing or double slashes
        if rng.random() < 0.1 and i in (0, depth-1):
            segs.append("")
        else:
            segs.append(make_segment(rng))
    topic = SEG_SEP.join(segs)
    # Randomly add a leading slash to create absolute topics
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and not topic.startswith(SEG_SEP):
        topic = SEG_SEP + topic
    # Randomly add trailing slash (allowed, denotes empty last level)
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and not topic.endswith(SEG_SEP):
        topic = topic + SEG_SEP
    return topic

def make_topic_filter(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Wildcards allowed: '+' single-level, '#" multi-level (must be last token, alone in its segment)
    depth = rng.choices([1,2,3,4,5,6], weights=[2,3,3,2,1,1], k=1)[0]
    segs: List[str] = []
    has_hash = False
    for i in range(depth):
        if not has_hash:
            roll = rng.random()
            if roll < 0.2:
                segs.append("+")
            elif roll < 0.25 and i == depth-1:
                segs.append("#")
                has_hash = True
            else:
                segs.append(make_segment(rng))
        else:
            # If '#' already used, remaining segments must not exist; ensure it's last
            break
    topic = SEG_SEP.join(segs)
    # Optional leading slash
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and not topic.startswith(SEG_SEP):
        topic = SEG_SEP + topic
    return topic

def make_payload(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 1024) -> bytes:
    # The stub truncates payload to 1024, so we keep within that. Add some newlines/tabs to vary.
    length = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    if length == 0:
        return b""
    s = "".join(rng.choice(PAYLOAD_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")


def encode_entry(kind: int, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # [kind:1][len:2-le][data][NUL]
    if len(data) > 65533:
        data = data[:65533]
    return bytes([kind]) + struct.pack("<H", len(data)) + data + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Generate a mix of entries. Ensure at least one publish topic, one filter, one payload.
    publish_count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    filter_count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    payload_count = rng.randint(1, 4)

    for _ in range(publish_count):
        t = make_topic_publish(rng).encode("utf-8")
        entries.append(encode_entry(0, t))
    for _ in range(filter_count):
        t = make_topic_filter(rng).encode("utf-8")
        entries.append(encode_entry(1, t))
    for _ in range(payload_count):
        p = make_payload(rng)
        entries.append(encode_entry(2, p))

    # Add some edge-case topics: very short, very long, leading/trailing slashes, deep hierarchy
    edge_topics: List[str] = []
    edge_topics.append("a")
    edge_topics.append("/")
    edge_topics.append("//double//slash//")
    edge_topics.append("home/+/sensor/#")  # filter edge
    # deep hierarchy without wildcards
    deep = "/" + "/".join("lvl" + str(i) for i in range(1, rng.randint(8,12)))
    edge_topics.append(deep)

    for s in edge_topics:
        kind = 1 if ("+" in s or "#" in s) else 0
        entries.append(encode_entry(kind, s.encode("utf-8")))

    # Shuffle entries for variety
    rng.shuffle(entries)

    # Prepend count byte (capped to 255)
    count = min(len(entries), 255)
    blob = bytes([count]) + b"".join(entries[:count])

    # Ensure total size <= 4096; if larger, trim entries conservatively
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Trim by reducing entries
        trimmed = []
        total = 1  # for count
        for e in entries:
            if total + len(e) > MAX_TOTAL:
                break
            trimmed.append(e)
            total += len(e)
        blob = bytes([len(trimmed)]) + b"".join(trimmed)

    return blob

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: Generate valid buffers for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME used as MQTT topic and payload
# in MqttClient_Publish and MqttClient_Publish_ex stubs.
# We will emit a bytes blob that contains two length-prefixed UTF-8 strings:
# [u16-be topic_len][topic_bytes][u16-be payload_len][payload_bytes]
#
# The fuzzer harness is expected to extract strings from the provided buffer.
# While we don't know its exact extraction format, providing a self-describing
# binary that starts with readable topic/payload strings maximizes the chance
# of meaningful FUZZ_PARAM_STR content. The topic will be a valid MQTT topic
# (with and without wildcards) and the payload is arbitrary binary or UTF-8.
# We keep total size <= 4096.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_PAYLOAD = 1024  # stubs clamp to 1024
MAX_TOPIC = 256

# Some interesting topic building blocks
BASIC_TOPICS = [
    "sensors/temp",
    "sensors/humidity",
    "home/livingroom/light",
    "devices/+/status",
    "devices/+/telemetry",
    "devices/device42/commands",
    "a/b/c",
    "$SYS/broker/uptime",
    "test",
    "test/retain",
]

# Topics with varying depth/characters, including edge and unicode (valid UTF-8)
UNICODE_SEGMENTS = [
    "室温", "привет", "Δοκιμή", "測試", "μqtt", "éclair",
]

# Payload templates that are valid UTF-8 JSON or text; we will also add binary variants
TEXT_PAYLOADS = [
    "hello world",
    "{\"msg\":\"hello\",\"n\":%d}",
    "{\"status\":\"ok\",\"ts\":%d}",
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
    "",  # empty payload (valid)
]

CONTENT_TYPES = [
    "text/plain; charset=utf-8",
    "application/json",
    "application/octet-stream",
]

def _rand_rng(seed: int) -> random.Random:
    return random.Random(seed)

def build_topic(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly choose a base or construct a topic
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        topic = rng.choice(BASIC_TOPICS)
    else:
        # Compose segments 1..6
        segs: List[str] = []
        n = rng.randint(1, 6)
        for i in range(n):
            kind = rng.randint(0, 9)
            if kind <= 4:
                seg = f"seg{rng.randint(0, 999)}"
            elif kind == 5:
                seg = "+"  # single-level wildcard (valid in SUB, but allowed string)
            elif kind == 6:
                # multi-level wildcard only valid at end; we place at end sometimes
                seg = "#"
            elif kind == 7:
                seg = rng.choice(UNICODE_SEGMENTS)
            elif kind == 8:
                seg = f"device{rng.randint(1, 1000)}"
            else:
                seg = f"room{rng.randint(1, 50)}"
            segs.append(seg)
        topic = "/".join(segs)
        # Ensure # only at end if present
        if "#" in segs and segs[-1] != "#":
            # move any '#' to end
            segs = [s for s in segs if s != "#"] + ["#"]
            topic = "/".join(segs)
        # Avoid empty string
        if not topic:
            topic = "test"
    # Ensure length constraint
    if len(topic.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_TOPIC:
        # Trim by segments
        parts = topic.split('/')
        while parts and len("/".join(parts).encode('utf-8')) > MAX_TOPIC:
            parts.pop()
        topic = "/".join(parts) or "test"
    return topic

def build_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    mode = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if mode <= 2:
        # Text/JSON
        template = rng.choice(TEXT_PAYLOADS)
        if "%d" in template:
            text = template % rng.randint(0, 1_000_000)
        else:
            text = template
        # Occasionally add a content-type header-like preface
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            ct = rng.choice(CONTENT_TYPES)
            text = f"CT:{ct}\n" + text
        data = text.encode('utf-8')
    elif mode == 3:
        # Repeating pattern binary
        pat = bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))])
        count = rng.randint(1, max(1, (MAX_PAYLOAD // max(1, len(pat)))))
        data = (pat * count)[:MAX_PAYLOAD]
    elif mode == 4:
        # Incrementing bytes
        start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        length = rng.randint(0, MAX_PAYLOAD)
        data = bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(length)))
    else:
        # Mixed ASCII and binary
        ascii_part = ("data-" + str(rng.randint(0, 1_000_000))).encode('ascii')
        bin_part = os.urandom(rng.randint(0, 64))
        repeat = rng.randint(1, 8)
        data = (ascii_part + b"|" + bin_part) * repeat
        data = data[:MAX_PAYLOAD]
    # Ensure within limit
    if len(data) > MAX_PAYLOAD:
        data = data[:MAX_PAYLOAD]
    return data

def pack_len_prefixed(topic: str, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    t = topic.encode('utf-8')
    if len(t) > MAX_TOPIC:
        t = t[:MAX_TOPIC]
    if len(payload) > MAX_PAYLOAD:
        payload = payload[:MAX_PAYLOAD]
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += struct.pack('>H', len(t))
    buf += t
    buf += struct.pack('>H', len(payload))
    buf += payload
    # Keep total under cap
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_TOTAL])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = _rand_rng(seed)
    topic = build_topic(rng)
    payload = build_payload(rng)
    return pack_len_prefixed(topic, payload)

# Strategy: Emit a sequence of host strings separated by newlines, followed by a small trailer of

def rand_label(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=20):
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)

    s = [rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)]

        s.append(rng.choice(DNS_LABEL_CHARS))

def rand_domain(rng: random.Random):

def gen_ipv4(rng: random.Random):

        (10, rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(1, 254)),
        (172, rng.randint(16, 31), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(1, 254)),
        (192, 168, rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(1, 254)),
        (rng.randint(1, 223), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(1, 254)),
        (224, rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(0, 255)),  # multicast
    ]
    a = rng.choice(choices)
    return "%d.%d.%d.%d" % a


def gen_ipv6_variants(rng: random.Random):
    # produce a few different textual presentations
    addr = ipaddress.IPv6Address(rng.getrandbits(128))
    variants = set()
    variants.add(str(addr))  # compressed
    variants.add(addr.exploded)  # full
    # embed IPv4-mapped sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        v4 = ipaddress.IPv4Address(rng.getrandbits(32))
        v6 = ipaddress.IPv6Address(int(ipaddress.IPv6Address('::ffff:0:0')) | int(v4))
        variants.add(str(v6))
    return list(variants)


def pack_u32_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    x &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return bytes((x & 0xFF, (x >> 8) & 0xFF, (x >> 16) & 0xFF, (x >> 24) & 0xFF))


def build_hosts(rng: random.Random):
    hosts = []
    # Include curated sets
    hosts.extend(COMMON_HOSTS)
    hosts.extend(PUNYLIKE)
    hosts.extend(SPECIALS)
    # Random domains
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        hosts.append(rand_domain(rng))
    # IPv4 samples
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        hosts.append(gen_ipv4(rng))
    # IPv6 samples
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        hosts.extend(gen_ipv6_variants(rng))
    # Deep subdomain and long label case within 63-char label and total length reasonable
    long_label = 'a' * 63
    deep = '.'.join([rand_label(rng, 3, 8) for _ in range(8)]) + ".com"
    hosts.append(f"{long_label}.example.com")
    hosts.append(deep)
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for h in hosts:
        if h not in seen:
            seen.add(h)
            uniq.append(h)
    # Shuffle to vary
    rng.shuffle(uniq)
    # Ensure none exceed 128 (stub truncates), keep already under typical limits
    uniq = [h[:128] for h in uniq]
    return uniq


def build_trailer_uints(rng: random.Random):
    # Provide three 32-bit values for successive FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) calls in stub
    # 1) Port seeds (masked to 16-bit in stub)
    # 2) Timeout seeds (mod 2000 in stub)
    # 3) TLS use flag seed (bit0 used in stub)
    port_seed = rng.randint(0, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    timeout_seed = rng.randint(0, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    tls_seed = rng.randint(0, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return pack_u32_le(port_seed) + pack_u32_le(timeout_seed) + pack_u32_le(tls_seed)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    hosts = build_hosts(rng)
    # Join hosts as separate FUZZ_PARAM_STR supplies; typical harness consumes sequentially
    body = ('\n'.join(hosts)).encode('utf-8')
    trailer = build_trailer_uints(rng)
    data = body + b"\n" + trailer
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data
